source_text:
Ἐπεὶ δὲ
ἤκουσα ὅτι τινὲς ἐγόγγυσαν καθ' ἡμῶν, ὅτι ἐν τῷ διαβαίνειν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸν ἅγιον
τόπον τῆς Βεθῆλ τοῦ συναγελασθῆναι τῇ σῇ τιμιότητι ὡς ἤλθομεν εἰς τὴν κώμην
τὴν λεγομένην Ἀναυθά, θεασάμενοι λύχνον καιόμενον καὶ ἐρωτήσαντες ἔγνωμεν
ἐκκλησίαν εἶναι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ, εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ τοῦ εὐχὴν ἐπιτελέσαι εὕρομεν βῆλον
ἐν τῇ θύρᾳ βαπτὸν ἐν ᾧ ἐζωγράφητο ἀνδροείκελόν τι εἰδωλοειδές, ὃ ἔλεγον τάχα ὅτι

Χριστοῦ ἦν τὸ ἐκτύπωμα ἢ ἑνὸς τῶν ἁγίων οὐ γὰρ μέμνημαι ἐγὼ θεασάμενος, καὶ
εἰδὼς ὅτι μύσος ἐστὶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ τοιαῦτα εἶναι, διέρρηξα αὐτὸ καὶ συνεβούλευσα
ἀμφιάσαι ἐν αὐτῷ πένητα τελευτήσαντα, οἱ δὲ γογγύσαντες ἔλεγον· "ἔδει αὐτὸν
ἀλλάξαι ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων τὸ βῆλον πρινὴ αὐτὸ σχίσῃ", καίτοιγε ἐμοῦ ὑποσχομένου ὅτι
ἀντ' αὐτοῦ ἀπο 283 στελῶ ἕτερον, ἐβράδυνα δὲ τοῦ ἀποστεῖλαι διὰ τὸ ἀναγκαῖόν με
thought_title: Tearing the painted curtain at Anautha
orientation: Epiphanius is recounting to John what happened when he entered a church at the village of Anautha on his way to Bethel.
pass_a_gloss: But since I heard that some grumbled against us, that while we were crossing to the holy place of Bethel to gather together with your honor, when we came into the village called Anautha, having seen a lamp burning and having asked we learned that there was a church in the place, and entering to complete a prayer we found a curtain at the door, dyed, on which had been painted some human image, like an idol, which they were saying perhaps that it was a representation of Christ or of one of the saints, for I do not remember having seen it, and knowing that it is an abomination in church for such things to be, I tore it and advised to wrap in it a poor man who had died, but the ones who grumbled were saying: "He ought to have exchanged the curtain from his own resources before he tore it", although I had promised that in its place I would send another, but I delayed to send it because of the necessity for me

choices.why: keeps the two adjectives distinct and in source order; 'some' preserves the indefinite τι
neutral term for a depicted likeness, matching the uncertainty of what was painted

choices.term: μύσος ἐστὶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ τοιαῦτα εἶναι
choices.english: it is an abomination in church for such things to be
choices.why: preserves the impersonal construction and the infinitive clause exactly
rejected: such things are an abomination in the church
it is defilement for such things to be in church

choices.term: ἔδει αὐτὸν ἀλλάξαι ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων τὸ βῆλον πρινὴ αὐτὸ σχίσῃ
choices.english: He ought to have exchanged the curtain from his own resources before he tore it
choices.why: keeps the direct speech as a past obligation with the temporal clause; 'exchanged' for ἀλλάξαι rather than 'replaced' to preserve the sense of giving something in return
rejected: He should have replaced the curtain from his own means before tearing it
It was necessary for him to change the curtain from his own before he split it

choices.term: ἐβράδυνα δὲ τοῦ ἀποστεῖλαι διὰ τὸ ἀναγκαῖόν με
choices.english: but I delayed to send it because of the necessity for me
choices.why: literal rendering of the genitive articular infinitive and the incomplete final clause; the sentence breaks off in the source
rejected: but I was slow to send because of the necessity I had
but I delayed sending because it was necessary for me

pass_b_english: But since I have heard that some people grumbled against us, saying that while we were crossing to the holy place of Bethel to gather together with your honor, when we came to the village called Anautha, we saw a lamp burning and asked about it and learned that there was a church in that place. When we entered to offer a prayer, we found at the door a dyed curtain on which had been painted some human image, idol-like, which they said was perhaps a representation of Christ or of one of the saints—for I do not remember what I saw. And knowing that it is an abomination in church for such things to be, I tore it and advised that they wrap a poor dead person in it. But those who grumbled said, "He ought to have exchanged the curtain from his own resources before he tore it." And yet I had promised that I would send another in its place, but I delayed to send it because of the necessity for me to travel.
notes: The source text breaks off mid-sentence at 'διὰ τὸ ἀναγκαῖόν με' (because of the necessity for me), continuing in the next section with 'ζητεῖν'.
The text contains 'ἀπο 283 στελῶ' with what appears to be a page number '283' inserted in the middle of the word ἀποστελῶ.

last_rejected.quote: exchanged the curtain from his own resources
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλάξαι ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων τὸ βῆλον
last_rejected.why: 'ἀλλάξαι' means 'replace', not 'exchange'; grumblers say he should have provided a replacement first, not swapped it.
last_rejected.fix: replaced the curtain from his own resources
last_rejected.ruling: ἀλλάξαι can mean 'change/replace'; 'exchanged from his own resources' conveys replacing at own expense adequately.

problems.why: Same person addressed as 'papa' then 'your honor'; reader may miss continuity.
problems.fix: Use one title or gloss 'papa' as honorific.

problems.quote: He ought to have exchanged the curtain from his own resources before he tore it
problems.why: Quoted speech lacks clear attribution; grumblers' words merge with narrative.
problems.fix: Add 'they said' or set as direct quotation clearly.

problems.quote: but I delayed to send it because of the necessity for me
problems.why: Sentence breaks off incomplete, leaving thought hanging.
problems.fix: Indicate textual lacuna or supply missing conclusion.

problems.why: Ambiguous whether curtain resembles idol or is idol-like abomination.

problems.quote: because of the necessity for me
problems.why: Sentence is incomplete; 'for me' dangles without a verb or completion.
problems.fix: Complete the sentence, e.g., 'because of the necessity for me to travel.'

problems.quote: But those who grumbled said, "He ought to have exchanged the curtain from his own resources before he tore it."
problems.why: Reader may not immediately distinguish whether this is Epiphanius quoting critics or the editor paraphrasing.
problems.fix: Clarify that Epiphanius is quoting his critics' words.
